newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court clears sale of Nazi memorabilia.
newsitem.headline: French court clears sale of Nazi memorabilia.

text.p: The Paris appeals court has cleared the marketing of Nazi memorabilia, saying it did not break French laws on racism as long as no propaganda was sold with the insignia.
In a ruling released on Wednesday, the court struck down a lower court injunction ordering French businessman Jean-Marc Fournier to stop selling Nazi insignia, SS uniforms and busts of Adolf Hitler.

"The marketing of such items is legal because it is not accompanied by a racist message," the court said. It noted Fournier's list of memorabilia also included insignia of World War Two forces which fought the Nazis.
The French Jewish Students Union, which took the legal action against Fournier, expressed shock and said it would appeal to the Supreme Court.
